children: Shares of nuclear energy companies surged Friday as investors responded to quarterly results from Oklo
and NuScale Power
, fueling a broader rebound in companies tied to the development of advanced reactors and the growing electricity demands of artificial intelligence.
Oklo
jumped about 23%, while NuScale Power
rose 16%. Nano Nuclear Energy
gained 15%, Centrus Energy
climbed 17%, Vistra
advanced 11% and X-Energy
added 16%.

The rally highlighted investors' continuing interest in nuclear power as technology companies seek reliable electricity for energy-intensive AI data centers. However, the sharp gains also followed substantial declines in several nuclear stocks, suggesting that bargain hunting and a reversal of bearish positioning contributed to Friday's advance.
Oklo results provide catalyst
Oklo

reported a third-quarter net loss of $41.7 million, narrower than analysts had expected, while revenue totaled $1.86 million. The company ended September with approximately $3.13 billion in cash, providing funding for its reactor development plans.
The company also reported progress on its Aurora nuclear project in Idaho, where structural construction work has begun and the Department of Energy has approved a preliminary safety analysis. Oklo
is targeting initial operations in 2028 to 2029, although regulatory approvals, construction costs and financing remain significant uncertainties.
NuScale

, which released quarterly results November 5, reported a loss of 11 cents per share, smaller than analysts anticipated. The company also pointed to progress toward manufacturing reactor components through an agreement with South Korea's Doosan Enerbility. Its quarterly revenue declined to $281,000.
Uranium suppliers, power producers
Centrus Energy

, which supplies nuclear fuel and is expanding domestic uranium-enrichment capacity, benefited from company-specific developments as well as the sector rebound. Roth Capital upgraded the stock to Buy from Neutral with a $115 price target. Centrus also recently reported progress manufacturing centrifuges used to produce enriched uranium, an essential fuel for nuclear reactors.

Centrus reported third-quarter revenue of $55.5 million, down from $74.9 million a year earlier. Although reported net income increased to $31.6 million, the company recorded an adjusted net loss of $9.4 million. Its backlog of low-enriched uranium and higher-enrichment fuel contracts reached $5.4 billion, including contingent orders.
Vistra's

advance followed its own earnings announcement. The electricity producer reported third-quarter adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $2.38 billion, exceeding analysts' expectations of approximately $2.1 billion. Executives said demand from data centers and other large electricity customers remained strong in Texas and the PJM regional electricity market. Vistra
also expressed confidence in securing additional nuclear-power supply agreements.
X-Energy
, which is developing high-temperature gas-cooled reactors, and Nano Nuclear

, which is pursuing smaller nuclear reactor designs, also participated in the rally. Their gains reflected renewed buying across advanced nuclear companies, although no comparable company-specific catalyst was established for either stock on Friday.
Election selloff adds to volatility

The gains followed a difficult week for nuclear and electricity-related stocks after Democrats won control of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections. Investors had grown concerned that changes in energy policy and greater regulatory scrutiny of data centers could delay power projects or increase development costs.
Vistra

had fallen approximately 14% on Wednesday, while other electricity producers also suffered sharp losses. Analysts at Raymond James subsequently suggested that investors may have overreacted to the election results, given the longer-term outlook for electricity consumption.
For investors, Friday's rally illustrated both the opportunities and risks in the nuclear energy sector. Established electricity producers such as Vistra

already generate substantial operating earnings, while companies developing next-generation reactors depend on future regulatory approvals, construction milestones and commercial contracts. Nuclear-fuel suppliers such as Centrus occupy another part of the industry, with demand tied to the expansion and operation of reactor fleets.
Despite its 23% gain, Oklo

remained approximately 67% below its level at the beginning of 2026. Its future performance will depend partly on turning proposed projects into operating reactors and binding electricity contracts, including its planned Ohio development associated with Meta Platforms

Friday's gains represented a combination of earnings-driven buying and a rebound from recent losses, rather than evidence that the nuclear industry's long-term financial and regulatory challenges had been resolved.

title: Nuclear stocks surge as Oklo results spark rally for reactors, uranium suppliers
